Under Kharija Taluk 349 belonging to Nitya Gopal Chowdbury and others there was a Sikimi Taluk comprising 10.53 acres of land in the name of Ramijemessa Shahebeni and others and under the Sikimi Taluk in Mouza Hossain pur there was a Dar Sikimi in respect of 3. 12 acres of land recorded in khatian No. 143 at rental of Rs. 15/- held by the plaintiffs. The owners of the Kharija Taluk put the Sikmi Taluk to sale in Rent Execution case No. 495 of 1950 and auction-purchased the same. After taking delivery of possession they filed non-Judicial Misc. Case No.2 of 1955 under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and annulled Darsikimi Taluk belonging to the plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs took settlement of 1.14 acres of land out of 12 acre of khatian No. 143 at a rental of Rs.6/- by a registered kabuliyat executed on 1.2.56 and registered on 3.2.56. The lands of khatian No. 143 were recorded in the last revisional settlement in khas of the Government who claimed to acquire the same as excess khas land of the owners of the Khatija Taluk. The Government issued a- Notice upon the plaintiffs for assessment of compensation treating them to be trespassers. Thereupon the plaintiffs instituted the suit. The Government defendant contested the suit contending, inter alia that the lease on the strength of which plaintiffs were claiming title was hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as null and void. TM disputed lands, therefore, continued to be the khas lands of the owners of the Kharija Taluk and the Government has rightly acquired them as excess land of the landlord under the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the lands have been correctly recorded in the name of the Government. In reply to the contention of the Government the plaintiffs took a stand that the lease obtained by the plaintiffs was saved by sub-section (3) of section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and was not hit by that section. The learned Munsif after holding trial decreed the suit He held the view that the lease of plaintiffs was protected by sub-section (3) of section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge who heard the appeal took the view that the, protection of sub-section (3) of section 75A was not available to the plaintiffs and allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved that plaintiffs have preferred this appeal. 

 "75A (1) On and from the date of publication of a notification under sub-section (3) of section 17 or under sub-section (1) of section 31,no person shall sublet let any land in his khas possession in the area to which such notification relates. 

 Admittedly the owners of the Kharija Taluk have made the suit land khas after annulling the Dar Shikimi Taluk and admittedly also by registered kabuliyat dated 1.2.56, the plaintiffs have taken settlement of the suit land from the owners of the Kharija Taluk, Sub-section (I) of section 75A prohibits subletting of any land in khas possession. Sub-section (2) provides that an) sub-letting made contravention of sub-section (I) shall be null and void Sub-section (3) which is the saving provision provides that nothing in sub-section(1) and (2) shall apply to the sub-letting of any land purchased by a landlord in execution of rent decree when such land in sublet at a rent more than the rent which was payable for such land by the outgoing tenant. It appears that this sub-section (3) relates to the question of sub-letting of a land purchased by a landlord in execution of a rent decree. It is evident that it contemplates a case where the landlord has acquired land in khas on the strength of purchase at a sale held in execution of a rent decree. This does not contemplate a case where the landlord has purchased s superior interest at a rent sale and has thereafter brought land in khas after annulling a sub- ordinate tenure under which the land was held. The instant case therefore does not come within the saving clause. Besides holding of khatian No. 1.43 comprises 3.12 acres of land. Only 1.14 acres out of 3.12 acres of the holding was sublet at a rate rent which is more the rate of rent of the khatian. On this score also the lease of the plaintiffs does not come within the ambit of the savings provisions. For the reasons stated above I am of the opinion that the lease dated 1.2.56 on tile strength of which the plaintiffs claim title in the disputed land is hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and is not saved by the provision of sub-section (3) of that section. The leaked Court of appeal below has taken a correct view of the law and has rightly dismissed the suit. I would, therefore dismiss this appeal. In the circumstances of this case I do not make any order as to costs.
